scope: Bounded review of ISO 32000-2:2020 §12.3.3 Document outline and §12.4.3 Articles, including linked tables, Table 31 /B, the current EC3 erratum relevant to article order, and implemented reader/UI consumers. This is not whole-clause certification.

features.source_location: Effective PDF source: physical pp.459–461, visible footer pp.444–446; §12.3.3 and Table 150 begin on printed p.444, Table 151 spans printed pp.445–446. EC3 consolidated text: doc/md/ISO_32000-2_sponsored_EC3.md around the Document outline heading and Tables 150–151. Root Outlines is optional; its Type, if stated, is Outlines. First/Last and Count semantics depend on whether open entries exist. Item lists are linked with First/Last/Prev/Next; Title and Parent are required, as are adjacent Prev/Next links, and child-list links apply where descendants exist.
features.assessment: The reader follows First/Next and exposes nested order; public query and panel consumers use that result. Prev, Last, Parent and root/item Type are producer-side structural constraints or redundant consistency statements. Tolerant reading and cycle/depth/item guards are reader robustness policy, not proof that malformed producer structures conform.

features.source_location: Printed pp.444–446 (physical pp.459–461). Title is required text string; Dest and A are mutually exclusive. Clicking visible item text activates its destination or action. The clause describes jump or action behavior, not a mandatory outline panel.
features.assessment: The public interaction path is exercised for a destination and a URI action; destination routing is compared against an independent page-tree walk. The panel itself is optional product UI, while activation behavior is stated for a visible item. Existing tests use real or hand-built valid PDFs, but the source-focused panel tests do not make every producer constraint a reader rejection rule.

features.source_location: Printed pp.444–445 (physical pp.459–460). Root Count cannot be negative; item Count sign represents open/closed and positive Count represents the number of visible descendants under the specified recursive counting procedure. A leaf need not state Count.
features.assessment: Reader computes visibility and the UI tests preserve identity/order while closing and reopening a subtree. The item count algorithm has a direct test; a file's stated count is not used as a substitute for computing the visible tree. Counts written by producers remain their conformance obligation.

features.source_location: Printed pp.445–446 (physical pp.460–461). F bit 1 selects italic and bit 2 bold; C is DeviceRGB and defaults to black. Unknown bits have no specified style meaning.
features.assessment: The model reads specified style flags and colour/default. Host drawing is presentation. No additional visual exactness claim is made here beyond model interpretation and the panel's existing output assertions.

features.source_location: Effective PDF source: physical pp.475–476, visible footer pp.460–461. §12.4.3 and Table 162 are on printed p.460; Table 163 continues on printed p.461. Threads is optional. If present, each thread's required indirect F identifies its first bead; beads require indirect N and V links closing the ring. Each bead requires indirect P and R. Thread /I information is optional and follows §14.3.3 syntax. EC3 consolidated source: doc/md/ISO_32000-2_sponsored_EC3.md around §12.4.3 and Tables 162–163.
assertions: crates/pdf-model/src/article.rs ring traversal, wrap, and malformed-cycle unit tests
features.assessment: Parser starts at F and follows N, stopping at a repeated object; V is not independently traversed because it is the redundant reverse-link constraint. Reader tolerates missing or invalid required fields as absent options; this is not producer conformance validation. Real producer corpus and exact-xref unit fixtures independently supplement the model tests.

features.source_location: Table 31 is printed pp.104–107 (physical pp.119–122); the /B row is printed p.106 (physical p.121). It describes /B as Optional, recommended if the page contains beads, with an array of indirect refs and says the information can be recreated from Catalog /Threads. §12.4.3 /B sentence is printed p.460 (physical p.475): its paragraph says a page with beads shall contain /B. Published order phrases conflict (Table 31 'natural reading order'; §12.4.3 'drawing order'). EC3 Issue #320 strikes 'natural' and replaces 'drawing' with 'reading'; the project records that amendment in ADR 0746. Order is now aligned under the erratum evidence; the presence language remains inconsistent between the clause paragraph and Table 31.
features.assessment: The array consistency function is only used by its own model tests; it is not a user-visible validation or rendering route. With one thread on a page it checks sequence using the #320 reading-order amendment. With multiple threads on the same page it checks membership as a documented implementation choice because no order among threads is stated. Missing /B returns None and is not surfaced as an error. This matches Table 31's explicit optional/recommended entry and avoids overstating the remaining source conflict as a reader behavior defect.

features.source_location: §12.4.3 printed p.460 (physical p.475): processors may provide navigation facilities to follow a thread. This is permission, not a mandatory UI surface. Table 163 R is the bead's page rectangle. §12.6.4.7 supplies a thread action route.
features.assessment: The optional feature is implemented: list selection composes the standard thread action and applies R via FitR; tests check both page and independently reasoned zoom geometry. UI choice and exact tab label are product decisions, not duties imposed by the clause. Next-bead traversal is modeled by Articles::next but no current host exposes a next-bead control; the clause permits navigation and does not require that particular control.
